title: Three-line deal anchor logic (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, engineer-friendly 3-line anchor and supporting micro-battlecard to use in fast discovery calls and pilot qualification. Goal is to give SEs and AEs a compact, repeatable script that ties business impact -> operational guardrails -> low-risk pilot ask. Not polished: this is a sketch for testing on 5 pilot conversations next week.

Core 3-line anchor (pick one variant depending on buyer):
- Business-first variant (for product/PM): "Reduce user-facing latency and inference costs by running a production-grade inference runtime with predictable per-token economics — we typically see 30–60% unit-cost improvement vs naive self-hosted GPU endpoints while meeting tail-latency SLOs. Pilot: 2-week pilot on a representative route."
- Platform-first variant (for infra/platform leads): "Give your teams a single runtime that standardizes inference across hosted, dedicated, and VPC modes so you avoid 3 different deployment patterns and custom tooling — that reduces operational toil and incident blast radius. Pilot: two apps on a team’s staging cluster for 10 business days."
- Compliance-first variant (for security/compliance): "Meet data residency and KMS requirements without rebuilding inference orchestration — we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit trails for inference requests. Pilot: small validated request set inside your VPC."

Micro-battlecard (1 side, SE pocket):
- "Elevator" proof: "Customers shipping at scale choose predictable serving to control $/MAU. We help mid-market and enterprise customers reduce per-token ops and SRE overhead while keeping latency guarantees."
- Quick numbers to cite (frame as typical results):
  * 30–60% lower per-token cost vs unmanaged GPU endpoints (prefix KV cache + batching);
  * 95th p50 latency parity with common self-host stacks when using dedicated pools + optimized kernels;
  * Pilot ramp: functional pilot in 5–10 business days, measurable metrics in 2 weeks.
- 3 technical win-lines:
  1) Transparent routing and fallback: route by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants.
  2) Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching reduce token compute dramatically for conversational flows.
  3) Dedicated capacity with burst lanes for predictable production throughput.

Objections and fast responses:
- "We can just run an endpoint on our infra." -> "Totally — most customers try that first. Two differences we see: (a) the unit economics and tail-latency behavior change as traffic scales; (b) you end up building routing/caching/rollout playbooks that we provide out-of-the-box. Pilot scope is designed to quantify those two deltas quickly.
- "How do you handle PII and KMS?" -> "We support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC-private deployments; we produce audit logs for every inference. For pilots we can run the route inside your VPC.
- "What about model quality/regressions?" -> "We tie quality monitoring to reproducible prompt sets and regression alerts; can run head-to-head evals as part of the pilot.

Pilot ask (clear, minimal):
- 1 production-like route (can be staging) that receives real user prompts (anonymized if needed).
- ~48–72 hours of traffic (or synthetic traffic that mimics your distribution) for baseline metrics + 10 business days of pilot to exercise fallbacks and rollouts.
- A single platform contact and one engineer for embedded handoffs.

Demo hooks and quick artifacts to show live:
- Latency/throughput dashboard (show 95/99 latency bands, per-route cost).
- Token-level cost waterfall (prefix cache hit rate, batching effectiveness).
- Failover demo: simulate capacity shortage -> automatic routing to quantized variant with preserved SLO.

Decision/fallback tree (one-page script for SE during discovery):
1) Is the primary buyer building product features or owning infra? -> route to Product/Platform variant of the 3-line anchor.
2) Are residency/compliance requirements present? -> propose VPC/private deployment pilot.
3) Is cost predictability the top concern? -> offer dedicated capacity commit vs hosted experiment to compare tail economics.
4) If they are unsure, propose a lightweight staging pilot with synthetic traffic to measure cost/latency deltas.

Suggested slide sketch (6 slides):
- Slide 1: One-line anchor + 2 supporting metrics (cost delta, latency parity) + pilot ask.
- Slide 2: How we differ from "just run an endpoint" (ops and economics).
- Slide 3: Pilot plan (what we measure, responsibilities, success criteria).
- Slide 4: Short technical architecture (runtime, routing, cache).
- Slide 5: Risk controls and compliance (KMS, audit logs, private options).
- Slide 6: Next steps & contact + quick checklist for kickoff.

Open questions / research items (to resolve before v0.1):
- Collect 3 anonymized case studies (mid-market + enterprise) that show cost delta numbers with similar workload shapes. We have internal notes but need permission to publish numbers.
- Standardize the pilot telemetry template: retain only key fields (route, p50/p95/p99, cost/unit, cache-hit-rate) for the SE dashboard.
- Pricing squeeze: define the guardrail around committed vs experimental pilot pricing.

Testing plan for this sketch:
- Try script on 5 incoming pilot discovery calls this week; capture what resonated and what stalled.
- SEs to note exact phrasing that moved platform vs product buyers.
- Iterate the one-liner and numbers after 5 conversations; produce v0.1 with slide pack.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Pull three anonymized examples from sales ops (ask Rosa).
- Draft 1-pager slide deck from the slide sketch (Evan to draft).
- Add short checklist for security team approvals for VPC pilots.

Related artifacts & references:
- Confluence draft for pilot gating: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/GTMA/three-line-anchor
- Jira epic for pilot framework: GTM-3421
- Slack thread with early SE feedback (see linked_artifacts)

Quick scripts (pick one for call):
- "If you had to pick one metric that matters to you in the next 60 days — is it cost per user, latency tail, or auditability? We’ll design the pilot to prove that signal in two weeks."
- "We’ll run a short head-to-head with your current endpoint and measure per-token economics and tail-latency — zero risk, and we own the instrumentation for comparison."

End of draft.

(Author note: keep this document short — it’s a live experiment to reduce friction in pilot qualification. We should not try to turn this into a full slide deck until iteration 0 feedback.)
